title: The Monkey and the Crab
summary: A kind animal grows food, but a mean monkey steals it every single day.
coverScene: A small red crab and a brown monkey sit together under a large green tree, sharing a bright red persimmon in the warm sunlight.

She picked it up.

She put it in her garden.

sentences.text: Long ago, in a quiet place near the sea, lived a small animal and another small animal.
The first animal was small and walked slowly, but she was kind and careful.
The second animal was quick and smart, but he often played games on others.
One day, the first animal found a bright red seed while walking along the beach.
She picked it up and thought that this would grow into a fine tree.
The animal took the seed home and planted it in her garden.
She watered it every day and sang to it softly.
Soon, a little tree began to grow, and after a few years, it bore fruit.
The fruit was big, red, and looked very sweet.
The animal was happy, but she knew she could not reach the fruit alone.
One morning, the second animal came by and saw the tree full of fruit.
He climbed up quickly and started to eat the sweetest ones.
The first animal called to him, asking him to please share some with her.
The second animal laughed and said that these were his now.
He threw a hard, green fruit at the animal and hurt her shell.
The animal was sad and angry, but she did not fight back.
She went to her friends—a small bug, a brown seed, and a stone bowl—and told them what happened.
They all agreed the second animal was bad and decided to help the first animal teach him a lesson.
The bug said that it would bite him when he was not looking.
The brown seed added that it would jump out and surprise him.
The stone bowl said that it would fall on him from above.
The animal thanked them and explained the plan.
The next day, the friends hid near the house.
When the second animal came home, he was happy and singing.
He did not see the bug, the brown seed, or the stone bowl waiting for him.
Suddenly, the bug flew at the second animal and bit his nose.
The animal cried out and tried to hit the bug, but he missed.
Then the brown seed rolled out and hit his foot, making him jump.
Before he could run, the stone bowl fell from the roof and landed on his head.
The animal was surprised and fell to the ground, touching his head.
The first animal came out and said that this is what happens when you are mean to others.
The second animal felt sorry and promised never to play games again.
He helped the animal pick the fruit from her tree and shared it with everyone.
From that day on, the second animal was kind to all his friends.
The animal accepted him, and they all lived happily together.
If the second animal had been kind from the start, he would have enjoyed the fruit without any trouble.
Which shows that friendship is more important than ego.
Every time the sun rose, the trees grew taller and stronger.
The local people often watched the garden with great joy.
They knew that goodwill always brings good results in the end.
Many months passed by, and the seasons changed from spring to summer.
The small animal continued to take care of her plants and animals around her.
Nobody in the town ever forgot the important lesson which was taught that day.
Life went on quietly near the beautiful blue sea.
If anyone visits the town today, they can still see the wonderful tree standing proudly in the garden.
The story remains a famous part of local history and brings joy to every child who hears it.

sentences.text: Long ago, in a quiet coastal settlement where the salt spray kissed the coastal vegetation, dwelt two very different creatures.
The first was a creature of deliberate, measured steps, possessing a gentle disposition and an infinite patience.
Her counterpart was a creature of restless energy, gifted with a sharp mind that he too often employed in malicious pranks.
While she moved through the world with mindful care, he darted about seeking whom he might manipulate next.
Their paths were destined to cross against the backdrop of an indifferent sea and an unchanging horizon.
One sunlit morning, while she strolled along the damp curve of the beach, her keen eye caught a flash of crimson in the sand.
It was a seed, exceptionally bright and perfectly formed, resting quietly among the scattered debris of the tide.
Not only did she pick it up with utmost tenderness, but she also perceived within its hard shell the promise of a magnificent tree.
She carried her precious discovery back to the sanctuary of her modest garden, cradling it as though it were a fragile secret.
There in the fertile earth, she planted the seed with deliberate grace, whispering quiet encouragement to the soil.
Day after day, she tended the spot with unwavering devotion, fetching cool water and singing low, melodic lullabies.
Scarcely had the seasons turned twice before a vigorous sapling broke through the surface, stretching upward with eager vitality.
As the years dissolved into memory, the tree matured into a magnificent specimen bearing fruit of astonishing size and brilliance.
Its globes of red flesh hung heavy from the branches, radiating a sweet fragrance that drifted across the neighborhood.
Though she rejoiced in her horticultural triumph, a quiet melancholy settled upon her when she realized her physical limitations.
It was precisely at this moment of vulnerable longing that her mischievous acquaintance happened to pass by the garden wall.
Noticing the laden boughs dripping with luscious fruit, his eyes widened with opportunistic greed rather than shared joy.
Before she could utter a single word of caution, he had scaled the trunk with agile leaps, plunging straight into the feast.
Selecting only the most opulent specimens, he devoured them with reckless abandon while scattering sticky rinds upon the ground.
Desperate to salvage some portion of her harvest, she called upward, politely begging him to cast down a share for her.
Instead of showing any measure of remorse, the trickster burst into harsh mockery, claiming the entire harvest as his rightful prize.
Only when she persisted did his amusement curdle into malice, prompting him to hurl a heavy, unripe fruit directly at her.
The hard projectile struck her protective shell with a dull crack, sending a sharp wave of pain through her weary frame.
Stunned and deeply wounded, she retreated into the shadows of her home, nursing both her physical injury and a profound sense of injustice.
Yet, rather than surrendering to despair, she resolved to seek justice through the collective solidarity of her truest companions.
She journeyed out to consult her most trusted allies: a resilient little bug, a dormant brown seed, and an old stone bowl.
Having listened to the harrowing account with mounting indignation, they unanimously agreed that the arrogant climber deserved a decisive lesson.
Scarcely had she finished speaking when the spirited bug volunteered to conceal himself near the hearth and deliver a stinging rebuke.
Not to be outdone, the brown seed declared that it would position itself near the threshold to trip the intruder.
Finally, the heavy stone bowl rumbled its willingness to tumble from the high roof and administer a definitive blow.
Having finalized their intricate strategy, the conspirators took up their designated positions as the afternoon sun began to wane.
The very next evening, the perpetrator returned home in high spirits, whistling a carefree tune without a single suspicion.
Little did he know that quiet vengeance awaited him in the warm gloom of the hallway, disguised as ordinary household objects.
As he stepped across the threshold, his mind remained entirely occupied with thoughts of his afternoon feast.
The stage was set for a reckoning that would permanently alter the balance of power in their small community.
Without a moment of hesitation, the vigilant bug launched himself from the shadows and delivered a sharp bite to the intruder.
Startled by the sudden assault, the visitor cried out in shock and swung wildly at the empty air.
Before he could regain his balance, the clever brown seed rolled swiftly across the floor and struck his heel with precision.
As he stumbled forward in confusion, the heavy stone bowl detached itself from the rafters and descended squarely upon his head.
Overwhelmed by the barrage of impacts, he collapsed onto the wooden floorboards, clutching his bruised skull in utter disbelief.
Emerging slowly from the doorway, the garden owner looked down at her humbled tormentor with calm dignity.
She reminded him that cruelty inevitably reaps its own bitter reward, while genuine community requires mutual respect and care.
Chastened by the experience and aching in every limb, the trickster finally understood the profound error of his ways.
Tearfully, he begged for forgiveness and swore an oath never to exploit another creature through selfish trickery again.
To prove his sincerity, he immediately set to work helping her harvest the remaining fruit for the entire neighborhood.
From that eventful day onward, a spirit of profound harmony replaced the friction that had previously defined their interactions.
No longer did the townspeople witness acts of spite; instead, they observed a touching friendship built upon accountability and shared labor.
Had the trickster chosen kindness from the beginning, he might have enjoyed the garden's bounty without enduring such a painful lesson.
Every morning as the sun climbed over the blue expanse of the ocean, the legendary tree grew taller and more resilient.
Generations of children would later gather beneath its shade, listening to the tale of how justice and friendship triumphed.
The seasons continued their eternal waltz, transforming spring blossoms into summer warmth and autumn gold.
Through every shift in the weather, the small animal maintained her peaceful existence, tending her plants with steadfast grace.
Nobody within the coastal settlement ever allowed the memory of that transformative afternoon to fade into obscurity.
Life flowed onward like the gentle tide, marked by quiet contentment and the comforting murmur of the nearby sea.
Even today, if a traveler wanders near the garden, they can still behold the proud branches whispering secrets to the wind.
